steps.label: Embedded Systems
steps.content:
3.1 Computer Architecture

Embedded Systems

Year 10

  • Today: about 20 minutes of notes. Then use your notes in Data Bridge.
  • The big question: why do so many machines have a small computer inside them?
Think → Pair → ShareA washing machine and a laptop both have a computer inside. Why can you play a game on the laptop, but not on the washing machine?Show the answer

Collect ideas. Today shows how the two computers are made for different jobs.

steps.label: What Is an Embedded System?
steps.content:
What Is an Embedded System?

  • A washing machine has a small computer inside it.
  • The computer has one job: to control the wash.
  • It reads the buttons, fills the drum with water, turns the drum and drains the water.
  • It never does any other job.
Inside the washing machine
  • buttons and a small screen
  • a small computer
  • a motor, a water pump, a heater
Embedded system: a computer system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function.
Dedicated function: one job, or a few jobs, that the device is made for. It does not change.

WHY? The machine only ever needs to do one job, so its computer is made for that one job.

steps.label: Your Notes: What Is an Embedded System?
steps.content:
Your Notes: What Is an Embedded System?

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

Embedded system
A computer system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function.
Dedicated function
One job, or a few jobs, that the device is made for. It does not change.
Example
A washing machine. Its embedded system controls the wash and does nothing else.

steps.label: General Purpose or Embedded?
steps.content:
General Purpose or Embedded?

LaptopWashing machine
Jobsmany different tasksone dedicated function
Softwarenew software can easily be installedcannot easily be reprogrammed
Extra devicesperipherals can be plugged in, such as a printer or a mouseno peripherals can be plugged in
Processora CPUa microprocessor
Wherea computer on its ownbuilt into a larger device
General purpose computer: a computer that can perform many different tasks, such as a laptop or a PC.
Peripheral: an extra device plugged into a computer, such as a printer or a mouse.

WHY? The user of a laptop decides its job. The maker of a washing machine decides its job.

steps.label: Your Notes: General Purpose or Embedded?
steps.content:
Your Notes: General Purpose or Embedded?

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

General purpose computer
A computer that can perform many different tasks, such as a laptop or a PC.
How it is different
New software can easily be installed. Peripherals, such as a printer, can be plugged in. It has a CPU.
WHY they are different
The user of a general purpose computer decides its job. The maker of an embedded system decides its job.

steps.label: Five Features of an Embedded System
steps.content:
Five Features of an Embedded System

FeatureWhat it meansWHY?
Dedicated functionIt does one job.The device only needs one job.
Dedicated hardwareIt only has the parts its job needs.Extra parts would cost money and use power.
MicroprocessorA CPU on one small chip.One chip is small and cheap.
Built into a larger deviceIt is inside the machine it controls.It must be next to the parts it controls.
Cannot easily be reprogrammedThe user cannot change its program.Its job never needs to change.
Dedicated hardware: only the hardware that is needed for the dedicated function.

WHY? Every feature comes from one idea: the system only ever does one job.

steps.label: Your Notes: Five Features
steps.content:
Your Notes: Five Features

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

Five features of an embedded system
1. Dedicated function. 2. Dedicated hardware. 3. A microprocessor. 4. Built into a larger device. 5. Cannot easily be reprogrammed.
Dedicated hardware
Only the hardware that is needed for the dedicated function.
WHY it has these features
It only ever does one job, so it only needs the parts and the program for that job.

steps.label: Why Use an Embedded System?
steps.content:
Why Use an Embedded System?

A freezer with a laptop inside
  • big, so it takes up space
  • costs a lot
  • uses a lot of power, all day and all night
  • a person must start the program
A freezer with an embedded system
  • small: it fits inside the freezer
  • cheap to make
  • uses little power
  • works automatically, with no person

WHY? It only has the hardware for one job. Fewer parts make it small, cheap and low power.

Think → Pair → ShareA freezer runs every minute of every day for years. Why does low power matter so much for it?Show the answer

Collect ideas: think about the electricity it uses over a whole year.

steps.label: Your Notes: Why Use an Embedded System?
steps.content:
Your Notes: Why Use an Embedded System?

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

Benefits of an embedded system
Small. Cheap to make. Uses little power. Works automatically, with no person.
WHY it has these benefits
It only has the hardware for one job, so it has fewer parts.

steps.label: Embedded or Not?
steps.content:
Embedded or Not?

Embedded systems
  • Domestic appliances (machines in a home): washing machine, freezer, microwave oven
  • Cars: the brakes, the air bags
  • Security systems: a burglar alarm, a security light
  • Lighting systems: street lights, traffic lights
  • Vending machines
General purpose computers
  • laptop
  • personal computer (PC)
  • tablet
  • smartphone: new apps can be installed
  • web server: runs many different programs
Test: Does it do one job, chosen by its maker? Then it is an embedded system.

WHY? A smartphone is small, but you can install new apps, so it can do many different tasks. Small alone does not make it embedded.

steps.label: Your Notes: Embedded or Not?
steps.content:
Your Notes: Embedded or Not?

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

Examples of embedded systems
Domestic appliances (washing machine, freezer, microwave oven), cars, security systems, lighting systems, vending machines.
NOT embedded systems
Laptop, PC, tablet, smartphone, web server.
WHY a smartphone is not embedded
New apps can be installed, so it can perform many different tasks.

steps.label: Exam Answers: Why Is It Embedded?
steps.content:
Exam Answers: Why Is It Embedded?

  • The exam asks: "The microwave oven is an example of an embedded system. Explain why it is an embedded system." [2]
  • 2 marks: write 2 features, about this device.
Earns the marks
  • It has a dedicated function: heating food.
  • It has a microprocessor.
Earns nothing
  • It is a computer.
  • It is a machine in a home.
  • Asked why something is not embedded? Turn the features round: It can perform many different tasks. New software can easily be installed.

WHY? A mark is for a feature that only an embedded system has. Every computer is a computer.

steps.label: Your Notes: Exam Answers
steps.content:
Your Notes: Exam Answers

What to do: open your notes (the pen icon at the top). Write the heading and the notes below. You will use these notes in Data Bridge.

Explain why it is embedded (2 marks)
Write 2 features, about the device. Example: It has a dedicated function: heating food. It has a microprocessor.
Explain why it is NOT embedded
It can perform many different tasks. New software can easily be installed.
WHY "it is a computer" earns nothing
Every computer is a computer. A mark needs a feature that only an embedded system has.
